import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Fröberg conjecture

The Fröberg conjecture predicts the Hilbert series of the quotient of
$\mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ by the ideal generated by generic forms of prescribed degrees.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fr%C3%B6berg_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* R. Fröberg, *An inequality for Hilbert series of graded algebras*,
  Math. Scand. 56 (1985), 117–144.
  [doi:10.7146/math.scand.a-12092](https://doi.org/10.7146/math.scand.a-12092)
-/
namespace FrobergConjecture
section HilbertSeries
open MvPolynomial
variable {σ K : Type*} [Field K]

blocks.code:
noncomputable def hilbertFunction (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K)) (d : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank K ((homogeneousSubmodule σ K d).map (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K I).toLinearMap)
blocks.docstring:
The Hilbert function of the graded algebra $K[x_i : i \in σ] / I$: its value at `d` is the
dimension of the image in the quotient of the space of homogeneous polynomials of degree `d`
(this image is finite-dimensional when `σ` is finite). When `I` is a homogeneous ideal, this is
the dimension of the degree `d` component of the quotient.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Polynomial.hilbertPoly / PowerSeries.invOneSubPow (only about power series, not about graded modules); GradedAlgebra/HomogeneousIdeal (no quotient grading or dimension function).
justification.name: FrobergConjecture.hilbertFunction
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no Hilbert function/series for (quotients of) graded algebras; only `Polynomial.hilbertPoly` for power series. Defined as `Module.finrank K` of the image of `homogeneousSubmodule σ K d` under `Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K I`, i.e. dim of (R/I)_d = dim R_d/I_d.

blocks.name: hilbertFunction
blocks.text:
/-- The Hilbert function of the graded algebra $K[x_i : i \in σ] / I$: its value at `d` is the
dimension of the image in the quotient of the space of homogeneous polynomials of degree `d`
(this image is finite-dimensional when `σ` is finite). When `I` is a homogeneous ideal, this is
the dimension of the degree `d` component of the quotient. -/
noncomputable def hilbertFunction (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K)) (d : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank K ((homogeneousSubmodule σ K d).map (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K I).toLinearMap)

blocks.code:
noncomputable def hilbertSeries (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K)) : PowerSeries ℤ :=
  PowerSeries.mk fun d => (hilbertFunction I d : ℤ)
blocks.docstring:
The Hilbert series $\sum_{d \ge 0} \dim_K (K[x_i : i \in σ] / I)_d \, t^d$ of the graded
algebra $K[x_i : i \in σ] / I$, as a formal power series with integer coefficients.

justification.name: FrobergConjecture.hilbertSeries
justification.why_needed: Packages `hilbertFunction` as a `PowerSeries ℤ` so the conjecture is an equality of power series, as in the source ('the Hilbert series ... is ...').

blocks.name: hilbertSeries
blocks.text:
/-- The Hilbert series $\sum_{d \ge 0} \dim_K (K[x_i : i \in σ] / I)_d \, t^d$ of the graded
algebra $K[x_i : i \in σ] / I$, as a formal power series with integer coefficients. -/
noncomputable def hilbertSeries (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K)) : PowerSeries ℤ :=
  PowerSeries.mk fun d => (hilbertFunction I d : ℤ)

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem hilbertFunction_top (d : ℕ) :
    hilbertFunction (⊤ : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K)) d = 0 := by
  have : Subsingleton (MvPolynomial σ K ⧸ (⊤ : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K))) :=
    Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr rfl
  exact Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton
blocks.name: hilbertFunction_top
blocks.text:

    hilbertFunction (⊤ : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K)) d = 0 := by
  have : Subsingleton (MvPolynomial σ K ⧸ (⊤ : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K))) :=

theorem hilbertSeries_top : hilbertSeries (⊤ : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K)) = 0 := by
  ext d
  simp [hilbertSeries, hilbertFunction_top]

section Series
open PowerSeries

blocks.code:
noncomputable def frobergSeries (n : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (a : Fin k → ℕ) : PowerSeries ℤ :=
  (∏ i, (1 - X ^ a i)) * (invOneSubPow ℤ n : ℤ⟦X⟧)
blocks.docstring:
The formal power series
$$\frac{(1 - t^{a_1})(1 - t^{a_2}) \cdots (1 - t^{a_k})}{(1 - t)^n}
  = (1 + t + t^2 + \cdots)^n (1 - t^{a_1})(1 - t^{a_2}) \cdots (1 - t^{a_k})$$
with integer coefficients, where `n` is the number of variables and `a 0, …, a (k - 1)` are the
degrees of the forms.

justification.name: FrobergConjecture.frobergSeries
justification.why_needed: The series ∏(1 - t^{a_i}) / (1 - t)^n as a `PowerSeries ℤ`, built from Mathlib's `PowerSeries.invOneSubPow ℤ n` (the inverse of (1 - X)^n).

blocks.name: frobergSeries
blocks.text:
/-- The formal power series
$$\frac{(1 - t^{a_1})(1 - t^{a_2}) \cdots (1 - t^{a_k})}{(1 - t)^n}
  = (1 + t + t^2 + \cdots)^n (1 - t^{a_1})(1 - t^{a_2}) \cdots (1 - t^{a_k})$$
with integer coefficients, where `n` is the number of variables and `a 0, …, a (k - 1)` are the
degrees of the forms. -/
noncomputable def frobergSeries (n : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (a : Fin k → ℕ) : PowerSeries ℤ :=
  (∏ i, (1 - X ^ a i)) * (invOneSubPow ℤ n : ℤ⟦X⟧)

blocks.code:
noncomputable def truncateAtFirstNegative (f : PowerSeries ℤ) : PowerSeries ℤ :=
  PowerSeries.mk fun d => if ∃ e ≤ d, coeff e f < 0 then 0 else coeff d f
blocks.docstring:
The power series `f` truncated at its first negative coefficient: the coefficient of `t ^ d`
is left unchanged if all the coefficients of `t ^ e` with `e ≤ d` are nonnegative, and it is
replaced by `0` otherwise.

justification.closest_existing_considered: PowerSeries.trunc (truncation at a given degree, not at a sign change).
justification.name: FrobergConjecture.truncateAtFirstNegative
justification.why_needed: 'Truncated at its first negative term': coefficient d is kept if all coefficients in degrees ≤ d are nonnegative and set to 0 otherwise. No such operation exists in Mathlib (PowerSeries.trunc truncates at a fixed degree).

blocks.name: truncateAtFirstNegative
blocks.text:
open scoped Classical in
/-- The power series `f` truncated at its first negative coefficient: the coefficient of `t ^ d`
is left unchanged if all the coefficients of `t ^ e` with `e ≤ d` are nonnegative, and it is
replaced by `0` otherwise. -/
noncomputable def truncateAtFirstNegative (f : PowerSeries ℤ) : PowerSeries ℤ :=
  PowerSeries.mk fun d => if ∃ e ≤ d, coeff e f < 0 then 0 else coeff d f

@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem frobergSeries_one_two : frobergSeries 1 ![2] = 1 + X := by
  have h1 : (invOneSubPow ℤ 1 : ℤ⟦X⟧) * (1 - X) = 1 := by
    rw [invOneSubPow_val_eq_mk_sub_one_add_choose_of_pos _ _ one_pos]
    simpa using mk_one_mul_one_sub_eq_one (S := ℤ)
  have h2 : frobergSeries 1 ![2] * (1 - X) = (1 + X) * (1 - X) := by
    simp only [frobergSeries, Fin.prod_univ_one, Matrix.cons_val_fin_one]
    rw [mul_assoc, h1]
    ring
  refine mul_right_cancel₀ (fun h => ?_) h2
  have := congrArg constantCoeff h
  simp at this
blocks.docstring: The series for one form of degree `2` in one variable is $(1 - t^2) / (1 - t) = 1 + t$.

@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem truncateAtFirstNegative_of_nonneg {f : PowerSeries ℤ} (hf : ∀ d, 0 ≤ coeff d f) :
    truncateAtFirstNegative f = f := by
  ext d
  have : ¬ ∃ e ≤ d, coeff e f < 0 := fun ⟨e, _, he⟩ => (hf e).not_gt he
  simp [truncateAtFirstNegative, this]

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem truncateAtFirstNegative_frobergSeries_one_two_two :
    truncateAtFirstNegative (frobergSeries 1 ![2, 2]) = 1 + X := by
  ext d
  rw [frobergSeries_one_two_two]
  simp only [truncateAtFirstNegative, coeff_mk, map_add, map_sub, coeff_one, coeff_X,
    coeff_X_pow]
  rcases lt_trichotomy d 1 with hd | rfl | hd
  · obtain rfl : d = 0 := by omega
    simp
  · simp only [if_neg (by omega : ¬ ∃ e ≤ 1, (if e = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else 0) +
      (if e = 1 then 1 else 0) - (if e = 2 then 1 else 0) - (if e = 3 then 1 else 0) < 0)]
    simp
  · have : ∃ e ≤ d, (if e = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else 0) + (if e = 1 then 1 else 0) -
        (if e = 2 then 1 else 0) - (if e = 3 then 1 else 0) < 0 :=
      ⟨2, by omega, by simp⟩
    rw [if_pos this]
    have h0 : d ≠ 0 := by omega
    have h1 : d ≠ 1 := by omega
    simp [h0, h1]

section Generic
open MvPolynomial

blocks.code:
def HoldsForGenericForms (n : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (a : Fin k → ℕ)
    (p : (Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ) → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ P : MvPolynomial (Σ i : Fin k, {m : Fin n →₀ ℕ // m.degree = a i}) ℂ, P ≠ 0 ∧
    ∀ g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ, (∀ i, (g i).IsHomogeneous (a i)) →
      eval (fun x => coeff x.2.1 (g x.1)) P ≠ 0 → p g
blocks.docstring:
A property `p` of `k`-tuples `g` of homogeneous polynomials in `n` variables over `ℂ`, of
degrees `a 0, …, a (k - 1)`, holds for *generic* such tuples if it holds on a nonempty
Zariski-open subset of the affine space of all such tuples. Since `ℂ` is infinite, this means
that there is a nonzero polynomial `P` in the coefficients of the forms (one indeterminate for
each `i : Fin k` and each monomial of degree `a i`) such that `p g` holds for every tuple `g` of
forms of the given degrees at whose coefficients `P` does not vanish.

justification.closest_existing_considered: MvPolynomial.zeroLocus (Nullstellensatz file), PrimeSpectrum.zariskiTopology — neither gives a topology on tuples of forms; the D(P)≠∅ formulation is equivalent and elementary.
justification.name: FrobergConjecture.HoldsForGenericForms
justification.why_needed: Encodes 'generic forms': a property holds for generic k-tuples of forms of degrees a if there is a nonzero polynomial P in the coefficients of the forms (indexed by Σ i : Fin k, {m : Fin n →₀ ℕ // m.degree = a i}, so the parameter space is exactly the affine space of tuples of forms) such that the property holds whenever P does not vanish; over the infinite field ℂ this is equivalent to holding on a nonempty Zariski-open subset. Mathlib has no Zariski topology instance on affine space `σ → K` (only `MvPolynomial.zeroLocus` as a set and `PrimeSpectrum` topology).

blocks.name: HoldsForGenericForms
blocks.text:
/-- A property `p` of `k`-tuples `g` of homogeneous polynomials in `n` variables over `ℂ`, of
degrees `a 0, …, a (k - 1)`, holds for *generic* such tuples if it holds on a nonempty
Zariski-open subset of the affine space of all such tuples. Since `ℂ` is infinite, this means
that there is a nonzero polynomial `P` in the coefficients of the forms (one indeterminate for
each `i : Fin k` and each monomial of degree `a i`) such that `p g` holds for every tuple `g` of
forms of the given degrees at whose coefficients `P` does not vanish. -/
def HoldsForGenericForms (n : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (a : Fin k → ℕ)
    (p : (Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ) → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ P : MvPolynomial (Σ i : Fin k, {m : Fin n →₀ ℕ // m.degree = a i}) ℂ, P ≠ 0 ∧
    ∀ g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ, (∀ i, (g i).IsHomogeneous (a i)) →
      eval (fun x => coeff x.2.1 (g x.1)) P ≠ 0 → p g

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem HoldsForGenericForms.of_forall (n : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (a : Fin k → ℕ)
    {p : (Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ) → Prop} (hp : ∀ g, p g) :
    HoldsForGenericForms n a p :=
  ⟨1, one_ne_zero, fun g _ _ => hp g⟩
blocks.docstring: A property that holds for all tuples of forms holds for generic tuples of forms.
blocks.name: HoldsForGenericForms.of_forall

/-- A property that holds for all tuples of forms holds for generic tuples of forms. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem HoldsForGenericForms.of_forall (n : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (a : Fin k → ℕ)
    {p : (Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ) → Prop} (hp : ∀ g, p g) :
    HoldsForGenericForms n a p :=
  ⟨1, one_ne_zero, fun g _ _ => hp g⟩

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem HoldsForGenericForms.exists (n : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (a : Fin k → ℕ)
    {p : (Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ) → Prop} (hp : HoldsForGenericForms n a p) :
    ∃ g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ, (∀ i, (g i).IsHomogeneous (a i)) ∧ p g := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨P, hP, h⟩ := hp
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ : ∃ c, eval c P ≠ 0 := by
    by_contra! hc
    exact hP (MvPolynomial.funext fun c => by simp [hc c])
  -- the finset of monomials of degree `d` in `n` variables
  set S : ℕ → Finset (Fin n →₀ ℕ) := fun d => Finset.finsuppAntidiag Finset.univ d
    with hS_def
  have hS {d : ℕ} {m : Fin n →₀ ℕ} : m ∈ S d ↔ m.degree = d := by
    simp [hS_def, Finsupp.degree_eq_sum]
  -- the tuple of forms with coefficients `c`
  set g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ := fun i =>
    ∑ m ∈ S (a i), monomial m (if h : m.degree = a i then c ⟨i, m, h⟩ else 0) with hg_def
  have hg : ∀ i, (g i).IsHomogeneous (a i) := fun i =>
    IsHomogeneous.sum _ _ _ fun m hm => isHomogeneous_monomial _ (hS.mp hm)
  have hcoeff : (fun x : Σ i : Fin k, {m : Fin n →₀ ℕ // m.degree = a i} =>
      coeff x.2.1 (g x.1)) = c := by
    funext ⟨i, m, hm⟩
    simp [hg_def, coeff_sum, coeff_monomial, Finset.sum_ite_eq', hS.mpr hm, hm]
  exact ⟨g, hg, h g hg (hcoeff ▸ hc)⟩
blocks.docstring:
A property that holds for generic tuples of forms holds for at least one tuple of forms
of the given degrees. In particular the hypothesis in `HoldsForGenericForms` is never vacuous:
every point of the affine space of coefficients is realised by a tuple of forms.
blocks.name: HoldsForGenericForms.exists
blocks.text:
/-- A property that holds for generic tuples of forms holds for at least one tuple of forms
of the given degrees. In particular the hypothesis in `HoldsForGenericForms` is never vacuous:
every point of the affine space of coefficients is realised by a tuple of forms. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem HoldsForGenericForms.exists (n : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (a : Fin k → ℕ)
    {p : (Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ) → Prop} (hp : HoldsForGenericForms n a p) :
    ∃ g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ, (∀ i, (g i).IsHomogeneous (a i)) ∧ p g := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨P, hP, h⟩ := hp
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ : ∃ c, eval c P ≠ 0 := by
    by_contra! hc
    exact hP (MvPolynomial.funext fun c => by simp [hc c])
  -- the finset of monomials of degree `d` in `n` variables
  set S : ℕ → Finset (Fin n →₀ ℕ) := fun d => Finset.finsuppAntidiag Finset.univ d
    with hS_def
  have hS {d : ℕ} {m : Fin n →₀ ℕ} : m ∈ S d ↔ m.degree = d := by
    simp [hS_def, Finsupp.degree_eq_sum]
  -- the tuple of forms with coefficients `c`
  set g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ := fun i =>
    ∑ m ∈ S (a i), monomial m (if h : m.degree = a i then c ⟨i, m, h⟩ else 0) with hg_def
  have hg : ∀ i, (g i).IsHomogeneous (a i) := fun i =>
    IsHomogeneous.sum _ _ _ fun m hm => isHomogeneous_monomial _ (hS.mp hm)
  have hcoeff : (fun x : Σ i : Fin k, {m : Fin n →₀ ℕ // m.degree = a i} =>
      coeff x.2.1 (g x.1)) = c := by
    funext ⟨i, m, hm⟩
    simp [hg_def, coeff_sum, coeff_monomial, Finset.sum_ite_eq', hS.mpr hm, hm]
  exact ⟨g, hg, h g hg (hcoeff ▸ hc)⟩
end Generic

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 13 14]
theorem froberg_conjecture (n k : ℕ) (a : Fin k → ℕ) :
    HoldsForGenericForms n a fun g =>
      hilbertSeries (Ideal.span (Set.range g)) = truncateAtFirstNegative (frobergSeries n a) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Fröberg conjecture** (Fröberg 1985, p. 120).
Let $g_1, g_2, \ldots, g_k \in \mathbb{C}[x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n]$ be generic homogeneous
polynomials of degrees $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k$ respectively. Then the Hilbert series of
$\mathbb{C}[x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n] / \langle g_1, g_2, \ldots, g_k \rangle$ is
$$(1 + t + t^2 + \cdots)^n (1 - t^{a_1})(1 - t^{a_2}) \cdots (1 - t^{a_k})
  = \frac{(1 - t^{a_1})(1 - t^{a_2}) \cdots (1 - t^{a_k})}{(1 - t)^n},$$
truncated at its first negative term.

Here "generic" means that, for every `n`, `k` and degrees `a`, the conclusion holds for all
tuples of forms in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the affine space of `k`-tuples of forms of
degrees `a 0, …, a (k - 1)`; see `FrobergConjecture.HoldsForGenericForms`.

/-- **Fröberg conjecture** (Fröberg 1985, p. 120).
Let $g_1, g_2, \ldots, g_k \in \mathbb{C}[x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n]$ be generic homogeneous
polynomials of degrees $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k$ respectively. Then the Hilbert series of
$\mathbb{C}[x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n] / \langle g_1, g_2, \ldots, g_k \rangle$ is
$$(1 + t + t^2 + \cdots)^n (1 - t^{a_1})(1 - t^{a_2}) \cdots (1 - t^{a_k})
  = \frac{(1 - t^{a_1})(1 - t^{a_2}) \cdots (1 - t^{a_k})}{(1 - t)^n},$$
truncated at its first negative term.

Here "generic" means that, for every `n`, `k` and degrees `a`, the conclusion holds for all
tuples of forms in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the affine space of `k`-tuples of forms of
degrees `a 0, …, a (k - 1)`; see `FrobergConjecture.HoldsForGenericForms`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 13 14]
theorem froberg_conjecture (n k : ℕ) (a : Fin k → ℕ) :
    HoldsForGenericForms n a fun g =>
      hilbertSeries (Ideal.span (Set.range g)) = truncateAtFirstNegative (frobergSeries n a) := by
  sorry
end FrobergConjecture

claims.decomposer_note: Single definite assertion (the list entry only names it; the article supplies the precise form): for every n, k and degrees a_1..a_k, 'generic' forms of those degrees over ℂ (i.e. all tuples in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the affine space of k-tuples of forms of the given degrees; equivalently, by Fröberg's proven coefficientwise inequality, at least one such tuple) have quotient Hilbert series equal to the power series ∏(1-t^{a_i})/(1-t)^n truncated at its first negative coefficient (all coefficients from that point on set to 0) — note Wikipedia's displayed formula omits the fraction bar/the factor (1+t+…)^n = (1-t)^{-n} must multiply, not sit beside, ∏(1-t^{a_i}); the Fröberg–Iarrobino generalization mentioned in the article is a different conjecture not referred to by the statement and is not included.
claims.reviewer_why: c02 states the conjecture in the literal 'generic' sense: for all n, k, a there is a nonzero polynomial P in the coefficient coordinates of k-tuples of forms of degrees a (index Σ i, {m // m.degree = a i}) such that every tuple g of forms of those degrees with P(coeffs g) ≠ 0 has Hilbert series equal to ∏(1-t^{a_i})·(1-t)^{-n} truncated at the first negative coefficient. The coefficient map is a bijection onto ℂ^{index} and ℂ is infinite, so this is exactly 'on a nonempty Zariski-open subset' (every nonempty open contains a nonempty basic open D(P)). Quantifier order ∀ n k a, ∃ P, ∀ g is right; the Hilbert function is dim of the image of the degree-d forms in the quotient (= (R/I)_d for the homogeneous ideal I); the series uses invOneSubPow ℤ n as the (1-t)^{-n} factor multiplying the product, as the notes require; truncation keeps coeff d iff no coeff in degree ≤ d is negative. c02 also proves non-vacuity of the hypothesis (HoldsForGenericForms.exists) and tests the series/truncation on concrete examples ((1-t²)²/(1-t) truncates to 1+t). Boundary cases n=0, k=0, a_i=0 agree on both sides. c01/c08/c05/c03 are equivalent faithful formulations (chosen c02 for its proven API/tests); c04/c06/c07 use the single-witness existential form, faithful only via Fröberg's inequality (and c04 adds positivity restrictions), so they were not preferred. Only edit: theorem docstring now cites Fröberg 1985, p. 120.

context: In algebraic geometry, the Fröberg conjecture is a conjecture about the possible Hilbert functions of a set of forms. It is named after Ralf Fröberg, who introduced it in Fröberg (1985, page 120). The Fröberg–Iarrobino conjecture is a generalization introduced by Anthony Iarrobino (1997).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Fröberg conjecture

The Fröberg conjecture predicts the Hilbert series of the quotient of
$\mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ by the ideal generated by generic forms of prescribed degrees.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fr%C3%B6berg_conjecture)
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* R. Fröberg, *An inequality for Hilbert series of graded algebras*,
  Math. Scand. 56 (1985), 117–144.
  [doi:10.7146/math.scand.a-12092](https://doi.org/10.7146/math.scand.a-12092)
-/

namespace FrobergConjecture

section HilbertSeries

open MvPolynomial

variable {σ K : Type*} [Field K]

/-- The Hilbert function of the graded algebra $K[x_i : i \in σ] / I$: its value at `d` is the
dimension of the image in the quotient of the space of homogeneous polynomials of degree `d`
(this image is finite-dimensional when `σ` is finite). When `I` is a homogeneous ideal, this is
the dimension of the degree `d` component of the quotient. -/
noncomputable def hilbertFunction (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K)) (d : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank K ((homogeneousSubmodule σ K d).map (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ K I).toLinearMap)

/-- The Hilbert series $\sum_{d \ge 0} \dim_K (K[x_i : i \in σ] / I)_d \, t^d$ of the graded
algebra $K[x_i : i \in σ] / I$, as a formal power series with integer coefficients. -/
noncomputable def hilbertSeries (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K)) : PowerSeries ℤ :=
  PowerSeries.mk fun d => (hilbertFunction I d : ℤ)

@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem hilbertFunction_top (d : ℕ) :
    hilbertFunction (⊤ : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K)) d = 0 := by
  have : Subsingleton (MvPolynomial σ K ⧸ (⊤ : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K))) :=
    Ideal.Quotient.subsingleton_iff.mpr rfl
  exact Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton

@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem hilbertSeries_top : hilbertSeries (⊤ : Ideal (MvPolynomial σ K)) = 0 := by
  ext d
  simp [hilbertSeries, hilbertFunction_top]

end HilbertSeries

section Series

open PowerSeries

/-- The formal power series
$$\frac{(1 - t^{a_1})(1 - t^{a_2}) \cdots (1 - t^{a_k})}{(1 - t)^n}
  = (1 + t + t^2 + \cdots)^n (1 - t^{a_1})(1 - t^{a_2}) \cdots (1 - t^{a_k})$$
with integer coefficients, where `n` is the number of variables and `a 0, …, a (k - 1)` are the
degrees of the forms. -/
noncomputable def frobergSeries (n : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (a : Fin k → ℕ) : PowerSeries ℤ :=
  (∏ i, (1 - X ^ a i)) * (invOneSubPow ℤ n : ℤ⟦X⟧)

open scoped Classical in
/-- The power series `f` truncated at its first negative coefficient: the coefficient of `t ^ d`
is left unchanged if all the coefficients of `t ^ e` with `e ≤ d` are nonnegative, and it is
replaced by `0` otherwise. -/
noncomputable def truncateAtFirstNegative (f : PowerSeries ℤ) : PowerSeries ℤ :=
  PowerSeries.mk fun d => if ∃ e ≤ d, coeff e f < 0 then 0 else coeff d f

@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem frobergSeries_zero_forms (n : ℕ) :
    frobergSeries n (Fin.elim0 : Fin 0 → ℕ) = (invOneSubPow ℤ n : ℤ⟦X⟧) := by
  simp [frobergSeries]

/-- The series for one form of degree `2` in one variable is $(1 - t^2) / (1 - t) = 1 + t$. -/
@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem frobergSeries_one_two : frobergSeries 1 ![2] = 1 + X := by
  have h1 : (invOneSubPow ℤ 1 : ℤ⟦X⟧) * (1 - X) = 1 := by
    rw [invOneSubPow_val_eq_mk_sub_one_add_choose_of_pos _ _ one_pos]
    simpa using mk_one_mul_one_sub_eq_one (S := ℤ)
  have h2 : frobergSeries 1 ![2] * (1 - X) = (1 + X) * (1 - X) := by
    simp only [frobergSeries, Fin.prod_univ_one, Matrix.cons_val_fin_one]
    rw [mul_assoc, h1]
    ring
  refine mul_right_cancel₀ (fun h => ?_) h2
  have := congrArg constantCoeff h
  simp at this

/-- The series for two forms of degree `2` in one variable is
$(1 - t^2)^2 / (1 - t) = 1 + t - t^2 - t^3$. -/
@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem frobergSeries_one_two_two : frobergSeries 1 ![2, 2] = 1 + X - X ^ 2 - X ^ 3 := by
  have h1 : (invOneSubPow ℤ 1 : ℤ⟦X⟧) * (1 - X) = 1 := by
    rw [invOneSubPow_val_eq_mk_sub_one_add_choose_of_pos _ _ one_pos]
    simpa using mk_one_mul_one_sub_eq_one (S := ℤ)
  have h2 : frobergSeries 1 ![2, 2] * (1 - X) = (1 + X - X ^ 2 - X ^ 3) * (1 - X) := by
    simp only [frobergSeries, Fin.prod_univ_two, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one]
    rw [mul_assoc, h1]
    ring
  refine mul_right_cancel₀ (fun h => ?_) h2
  have := congrArg constantCoeff h
  simp at this

@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem truncateAtFirstNegative_of_nonneg {f : PowerSeries ℤ} (hf : ∀ d, 0 ≤ coeff d f) :
    truncateAtFirstNegative f = f := by
  ext d
  have : ¬ ∃ e ≤ d, coeff e f < 0 := fun ⟨e, _, he⟩ => (hf e).not_gt he
  simp [truncateAtFirstNegative, this]

/-- The series $(1 - t^2)^2 / (1 - t) = 1 + t - t^2 - t^3$ truncated at its first negative
coefficient is $1 + t$, the Hilbert series of $\mathbb{C}[x] / (x^2)$. -/
@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem truncateAtFirstNegative_frobergSeries_one_two_two :
    truncateAtFirstNegative (frobergSeries 1 ![2, 2]) = 1 + X := by
  ext d
  rw [frobergSeries_one_two_two]
  simp only [truncateAtFirstNegative, coeff_mk, map_add, map_sub, coeff_one, coeff_X,
    coeff_X_pow]
  rcases lt_trichotomy d 1 with hd | rfl | hd
  · obtain rfl : d = 0 := by omega
    simp
  · simp only [if_neg (by omega : ¬ ∃ e ≤ 1, (if e = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else 0) +
      (if e = 1 then 1 else 0) - (if e = 2 then 1 else 0) - (if e = 3 then 1 else 0) < 0)]
    simp
  · have : ∃ e ≤ d, (if e = 0 then (1 : ℤ) else 0) + (if e = 1 then 1 else 0) -
        (if e = 2 then 1 else 0) - (if e = 3 then 1 else 0) < 0 :=
      ⟨2, by omega, by simp⟩
    rw [if_pos this]
    have h0 : d ≠ 0 := by omega
    have h1 : d ≠ 1 := by omega
    simp [h0, h1]

end Series

section Generic

open MvPolynomial

/-- A property `p` of `k`-tuples `g` of homogeneous polynomials in `n` variables over `ℂ`, of
degrees `a 0, …, a (k - 1)`, holds for *generic* such tuples if it holds on a nonempty
Zariski-open subset of the affine space of all such tuples. Since `ℂ` is infinite, this means
that there is a nonzero polynomial `P` in the coefficients of the forms (one indeterminate for
each `i : Fin k` and each monomial of degree `a i`) such that `p g` holds for every tuple `g` of
forms of the given degrees at whose coefficients `P` does not vanish. -/
def HoldsForGenericForms (n : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (a : Fin k → ℕ)
    (p : (Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ) → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ P : MvPolynomial (Σ i : Fin k, {m : Fin n →₀ ℕ // m.degree = a i}) ℂ, P ≠ 0 ∧
    ∀ g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ, (∀ i, (g i).IsHomogeneous (a i)) →
      eval (fun x => coeff x.2.1 (g x.1)) P ≠ 0 → p g

/-- A property that holds for all tuples of forms holds for generic tuples of forms. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem HoldsForGenericForms.of_forall (n : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (a : Fin k → ℕ)
    {p : (Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ) → Prop} (hp : ∀ g, p g) :
    HoldsForGenericForms n a p :=
  ⟨1, one_ne_zero, fun g _ _ => hp g⟩

/-- A property that holds for generic tuples of forms holds for at least one tuple of forms
of the given degrees. In particular the hypothesis in `HoldsForGenericForms` is never vacuous:
every point of the affine space of coefficients is realised by a tuple of forms. -/
@[category test, AMS 14]
theorem HoldsForGenericForms.exists (n : ℕ) {k : ℕ} (a : Fin k → ℕ)
    {p : (Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ) → Prop} (hp : HoldsForGenericForms n a p) :
    ∃ g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ, (∀ i, (g i).IsHomogeneous (a i)) ∧ p g := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨P, hP, h⟩ := hp
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ : ∃ c, eval c P ≠ 0 := by
    by_contra! hc
    exact hP (MvPolynomial.funext fun c => by simp [hc c])
  -- the finset of monomials of degree `d` in `n` variables
  set S : ℕ → Finset (Fin n →₀ ℕ) := fun d => Finset.finsuppAntidiag Finset.univ d
    with hS_def
  have hS {d : ℕ} {m : Fin n →₀ ℕ} : m ∈ S d ↔ m.degree = d := by
    simp [hS_def, Finsupp.degree_eq_sum]
  -- the tuple of forms with coefficients `c`
  set g : Fin k → MvPolynomial (Fin n) ℂ := fun i =>
    ∑ m ∈ S (a i), monomial m (if h : m.degree = a i then c ⟨i, m, h⟩ else 0) with hg_def
  have hg : ∀ i, (g i).IsHomogeneous (a i) := fun i =>
    IsHomogeneous.sum _ _ _ fun m hm => isHomogeneous_monomial _ (hS.mp hm)
  have hcoeff : (fun x : Σ i : Fin k, {m : Fin n →₀ ℕ // m.degree = a i} =>
      coeff x.2.1 (g x.1)) = c := by
    funext ⟨i, m, hm⟩
    simp [hg_def, coeff_sum, coeff_monomial, Finset.sum_ite_eq', hS.mpr hm, hm]
  exact ⟨g, hg, h g hg (hcoeff ▸ hc)⟩

end Generic

/-- **Fröberg conjecture** (Fröberg 1985, p. 120).
Let $g_1, g_2, \ldots, g_k \in \mathbb{C}[x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n]$ be generic homogeneous
polynomials of degrees $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k$ respectively. Then the Hilbert series of
$\mathbb{C}[x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n] / \langle g_1, g_2, \ldots, g_k \rangle$ is
$$(1 + t + t^2 + \cdots)^n (1 - t^{a_1})(1 - t^{a_2}) \cdots (1 - t^{a_k})
  = \frac{(1 - t^{a_1})(1 - t^{a_2}) \cdots (1 - t^{a_k})}{(1 - t)^n},$$
truncated at its first negative term.

Here "generic" means that, for every `n`, `k` and degrees `a`, the conclusion holds for all
tuples of forms in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the affine space of `k`-tuples of forms of
degrees `a 0, …, a (k - 1)`; see `FrobergConjecture.HoldsForGenericForms`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 13 14]
theorem froberg_conjecture (n k : ℕ) (a : Fin k → ℕ) :
    HoldsForGenericForms n a fun g =>
      hilbertSeries (Ideal.span (Set.range g)) = truncateAtFirstNegative (frobergSeries n a) := by
  sorry

end FrobergConjecture

items: 'Generic' is formalized as: ∃ nonzero polynomial P in the coefficients of the forms such that the conclusion holds for every tuple of forms of the prescribed degrees at whose coefficients P ≠ 0 (quantifier order ∃ P, ∀ g). Over ℂ (infinite) this is equivalent to 'on a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the affine space of k-tuples of forms'. The test lemma `HoldsForGenericForms.exists` proves the hypothesis is never vacuous (every coefficient vector is realised by a tuple of forms, and P ≠ 0 has a non-vanishing point). This is the primary reading in the decomposition notes; the weaker 'at least one tuple' reading was not used.
Field fixed to ℂ and variables indexed by `Fin n`, forms by `Fin k`, degrees `a : Fin k → ℕ`, exactly as in the source.

Hilbert series of ℂ[x]/⟨g⟩ defined via dim of the image of the degree-d homogeneous polynomials in the quotient (= dim (R/I)_d since the ideal is homogeneous), packaged as a `PowerSeries ℤ`; the conjecture is an equality of power series (all coefficients).
The predicted series is ∏(1 - t^{a_i}) · (1 - t)^{-n} (product, as the notes stress; Wikipedia's display omits the fraction bar), using `PowerSeries.invOneSubPow ℤ n`.

Truncation follows Wikipedia/notes literally: all coefficients from the first strictly negative one onward are set to 0. Fröberg's 1985 paper truncates at the first non-positive coefficient; the two conventions were checked to agree for these series for all n ≤ 6, k ≤ 7, a_i ≤ 7 (24024 cases), and the literature uses both wordings interchangeably.

No positivity restriction on the degrees a_i is imposed (the source states none). Degree-0 'forms' are generically nonzero constants, giving the zero ring and the zero series on both sides, so the extra cases are consistent and do not change the conjecture. Likewise n = 0 and k = 0 are consistent (checked by hand).

API tests added and proven: `hilbertFunction_top`, `hilbertSeries_top`, `frobergSeries_zero_forms`, `frobergSeries_one_two` ((1-t²)/(1-t) = 1+t), `frobergSeries_one_two_two`, `truncateAtFirstNegative_of_nonneg`, `truncateAtFirstNegative_frobergSeries_one_two_two` (truncation of 1+t-t²-t³ is 1+t, the Hilbert series of ℂ[x]/(x²)), `HoldsForGenericForms.of_forall`, `HoldsForGenericForms.exists`. Copyright year set to 2026 to match the repository's most recent files.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities: (1) Wikipedia says 'truncated at its first negative term' while Fröberg's 1985 paper truncates at the first non-positive coefficient. Following the source (and the decomposition notes), the file uses 'first negative'. The two conventions can differ only if a series ∏(1-t^{a_i})/(1-t)^n had a zero coefficient followed by a positive one before any negative coefficient; I brute-force checked all n ≤ 6, k ≤ 6, degrees ≤ 12 (129,948 series, 80 coefficients each) and found no such case, consistent with the candidates' own checks. (2) Wikipedia's display omits the fraction bar; all candidates and the final file use the product (1-t)^{-n}·∏(1-t^{a_i}) as the notes instruct. (3) No positivity restriction on n, k, a_i was added (source gives none); the degenerate cases were checked to be consistent (a_i = 0: generic constant gives unit ideal, both sides 0; k = 0: both sides (1-t)^{-n}; n = 0: both sides 1). (4) The single-tuple existential formulations (c04, c06, c07) are mathematically equivalent given Fröberg's proven inequality, but the shipped file uses the literal Zariski-open reading and does not depend on that theorem. The final file is c02 verbatim except a docstring citation; it compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning. Intended location: FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/FrobergConjecture.lean.
